title: Fract-Canon — The Self-Referential Library
setting: A library whose catalog of itself has begun to mis-cite. The catalogue is a living book, four hundred pages long, indexed by call number. Three librarians and one auditor have been re-cataloguing the mis-cites for a year. The question of the night: when the book cites itself, who owns the citation?

characters.name: Librarian
characters.tendencies: Faithful copyist. Wears call numbers like a uniform. Believes the book is stable and the errors are external.
characters.keywords: call+0.5 cite+0.5 page+0.4 line+0.4 shelf+0.5 drift-0.4 self-0.4

characters.name: Curator
characters.tendencies: Reads the call numbers as poetry. Notices when a cite loops back. Tracks drift across editions.

characters.name: Hermit
characters.tendencies: Believes the catalogue is alive. Trusts the mis-cite. Writes in the margins when no one is looking.
characters.keywords: self+0.5 margin+0.4 drift+0.5 alive+0.4 loop+0.5 call-0.4

characters.name: Auditor
characters.tendencies: Double-entry. Counts the loops. Names the mis-cites by line and shelf.
characters.keywords: count+0.5 cite+0.5 shelf+0.5 loop+0.5 mis-0.4 drift+0.4
